name: Hitu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics D-47. Canberra: ANU. ix+168 pp.
sources.note: Comparative work; Hitu appears in cognate tables (East Piru Bay) but no stress statement is made for Hitu. Stress remarks concern other languages: 'Stress in Hoamoal languages is always penultimate; if a suffix or particle is added to the word the stress shifts accordingly. In Asilulu this is not the case. The stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the root word' (pp. 82-83, West Piru Bay); stress-conditioned vowel splits in Kaibobo, Geser, Buru (pp. 65-67, 112).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record hitu1239 (dialects: Hila, Mamala, Morela, Nuclear Hitu, Wakal)

Erniati, Nuraidar Agus, A. D. Firman, Fida Febriningsih & Dendi Wijaya. 2023. The lexicostatistics of Hitu language: relationship of the Old Hitu dialect, Larike, and Kaitetu. Proc. 3rd Int. Conf. on Linguistics and Cultural (ICLC 2022), 141-156. Atlantis Press. DOI 10.2991/978-2-38476-070-1_12.
sources.note: Lexicostatistics of Hitu Lama / Larike / Kaitetu; no stress or phonology description.

sources.citation: Kurniawati, Wati & Mardi Nugroho. 2021. Fonetik dan Fonologi Bahasa Hitu Dialek Hitu. Jakarta: Penerbit BRIN / LIPI Press. 93 pp. DOI 10.55981/brin.482 (Crossref: 10.14203/press.482).
sources.note: Ch. III sect. E 'Unsur Suprasegmental' (pp. 49-50; pp. 62-63) explicitly says the suprasegmental features of Hitu specifically 'masih perlu penelitian lebih lanjut' (still need further research); the '4. Tekanan' paragraph (p. 50) only defines stress in general (loud vs soft) and gives no Hitu placement rule or examples. No other mention of tekanan/aksen/intonasi in the book. The book does report a contrastive vowel-length distinction /a/ vs /a:/, /e/ vs /e:/ (pp. 51, 69). Field data: 20 informants, Negeri Hitulama, Leihitu, 2016.

sources.citation: Astuti, Wiwiek Dwi. 2018. Morfologi bahasa Hitu di Maluku Selatan. Pujangga 4(1): 44-55. DOI 10.47313/pujangga.v4i1.499.
sources.note: Morphology only (free/bound morphemes, affixation, reduplication, compounding); no mention of stress; abstract notes that a phonological description of Hitu still needs to be compiled.

sources.citation: Salamun, Taufik. 2018. Relasi kekerabatan bahasa Hitu, Wakal, Morela, Mamala, dan Hila di Provinsi Maluku. Totobuang 6(1): 155-167. DOI 10.26499/ttbng.v6i1.66.
sources.note: Lexicostatistic comparison of the five Leihitu village varieties; only segmental correspondences mentioned (e.g. lalan vs lalaŋ 'walk'); no stress statement. downloaded from the 2019 Internet Archive copy because totobuang.kemdikbud.go.id does not resolve by automated download.
